update_variable_params(t: float, x_snapshot: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | None = None, scheduled_t: float | None = None) → None[source]

Update the variable parameters. Continuous runtime parameters are re-evaluated, while retained mode parameters are left untouched unless updated by boundary logic.

The RMS implicit solve needs two distinct time views. Continuous ramp-like parameters must be evaluated at the current local target time so the nonlinear solve sees the interpolated value inside the step. Historical scheduled step events, however, must keep the pre-event value on the sample aligned with the event instant and only latch afterwards. The optional scheduled_t argument therefore lets the caller decouple the continuous symbolic evaluation time from the scheduled event boundary time without duplicating the update logic.

Parameters:

  • t – Continuous symbolic evaluation time.

  • x_snapshot – Current state snapshot used by boundary logic.

  • scheduled_t – Optional time used by scheduled step logic.

Returns:

None.

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.Rms.problems.rms_problem_dae.build_inactive_bus_boundary_equations(bus: Bus, init_guess: Dict[int, float | int | complex | None]) → List[Expr][source]

Build algebraic boundary equations for one isolated inactive bus.

Inactive buses can remain stored in legacy grids without any connected active network element. Their RMS voltage variables are still present in the bus block, but nodal P/Q balances do not exist. Fixing those detached algebraic variables at the power-flow initial point removes them from the active DAE without adding electrical behavior to the network.

Parameters:

  • bus – Isolated inactive bus owning the RMS voltage variables.

  • init_guess – Global RMS initial-value lookup keyed by variable uid.

Returns:

One DC or two AC voltage boundary equations.

update_variable_params(t: float, x_snapshot: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | None = None, scheduled_t: float | None = None) → None[source]

Update the variable parameters. Continuous runtime parameters are re-evaluated, while retained mode parameters are left untouched unless updated by boundary logic.

The RMS implicit solve needs two distinct time views. Continuous ramp-like parameters must be evaluated at the current local target time so the nonlinear solve sees the interpolated value inside the step. Historical scheduled step events, however, must keep the pre-event value on the sample aligned with the event instant and only latch afterwards. The optional scheduled_t argument therefore lets the caller decouple the continuous symbolic evaluation time from the scheduled event boundary time without duplicating the update logic.

Parameters:

  • t – Continuous symbolic evaluation time.

  • x_snapshot – Current state snapshot used by boundary logic.

  • scheduled_t – Optional time used by scheduled step logic.

Returns:

None.

Build one vectorized layout from canonical mapped power references.

The layout exists for one compilation and is never attached to or persisted with the dynamic model. Static devices supply every bus index; the model mapping supplies only the canonical P/Q quantity semantics.

update_variable_params(t: float, x_snapshot: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]] | None = None, scheduled_t: float | None = None) → None[source]

Update the variable parameters. Continuous runtime parameters are re-evaluated, while retained mode parameters are left untouched unless updated by boundary logic.

The RMS implicit solve needs two distinct time views. Continuous ramp-like parameters must be evaluated at the current local target time so the nonlinear solve sees the interpolated value inside the step. Historical scheduled step events, however, must keep the pre-event value on the sample aligned with the event instant and only latch afterwards. The optional scheduled_t argument therefore lets the caller decouple the continuous symbolic evaluation time from the scheduled event boundary time without duplicating the update logic.

Parameters:

  • t – Continuous symbolic evaluation time.

  • x_snapshot – Current state snapshot used by boundary logic.

  • scheduled_t – Optional time used by scheduled step logic.

Returns:

None.

class VeraGridEngine.Simulations.Rms.problems.rms_problem_multilinear.MultilinearCpnApproximator(S: csc_matrix, Phi: csr_matrix)[source]

Bases: object

Implicit CP/CPN approximator for a sparse multilinear representation.

The exact multilinear residual is assumed to be represented as:

f(x) = Phi @ varphi(x)

where:

  • S has shape (n_vars, n_mon)

  • Phi has shape (n_eq, n_mon)

  • each column of S defines one multilinear monomial

The equivalent coefficient tensor H has shape:

(n_eq, 2, 2, …, 2)

with one binary basis mode [1, x_i] per variable. This class fits a CP/CPN approximation of H without ever constructing H explicitly.

The fitted CP tensor has factors:

factors[0] -> equation factor, shape (n_eq, rank) factors[i + 1] -> variable i factor, shape (2, rank)

Phasor RMS problem with multilinear-oriented utilities.

This class keeps the regular symbolic compilation from RmsProblemPhasor and adds lightweight operating-point extraction and small-signal helpers inspired by PolynomialMatrixBuilder but without SciPy dependencies.

Build (S, Phi) multilinear matrices from problem equations.

S encodes monomial structure (variables x monomials), Phi encodes equation coefficients (equations x monomials).

build_sparse_h_from_s_phi(zero_tol: float = 1e-12) → SparseCoefficientTensor[source]

Build the exact sparse coordinate representation of the coefficient tensor H.

The exact multilinear representation is:

f(x) = Phi @ varphi(x)

where:

  • S defines the monomial basis varphi(x)

  • Phi contains the equation-by-monomial coefficients

The tensor H has shape:

(n_eq, 2, 2, …, 2)

where:

  • mode 0 is the equation mode

  • mode i + 1 corresponds to the local basis [1, x_i]

Returns

SparseCoefficientTensor

Sparse coordinate representation of H.

evaluate_residual_from_cptensor(x: ndarray, cp_tensor: MultilinearCpTensor) → ndarray[source]

Evaluate the approximate residual from a CP tensor.

This implements:

q_r = prod_i (A_i[0, r] + A_i[1, r] * x_i) f = B @ (weights * q)

where:

  • B = factors[0]

  • A_i = factors[i + 1]

Parameters

x

Variable vector with shape (n_vars,).

cp_tensor

CP tensor representing the approximate coefficient tensor H.

Returns

np.ndarray

Approximate residual vector with shape (n_eq,).

exact_phi_from_s(x: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Evaluate the exact monomial basis vector varphi(x) from S.

The matrix S has shape:

(n_vars, n_mon)

Each column j of S defines one multilinear monomial:

varphi_j(x) = prod_i (S[i, j] * x_i + 1 - abs(S[i, j]))

If S[i, j] = 0, the local factor is 1. If S[i, j] = 1, the local factor is x_i. If S[i, j] = -1, the local factor is -x_i.

Parameters

x

Variable vector with shape (n_vars,).

Returns

np.ndarray

Monomial basis vector with shape (n_mon,).

exact_residual_from_s_phi(x: ndarray) → ndarray[source]

Evaluate the exact residual f(x) = Phi @ varphi(x).

This is the exact residual of the sparse multilinear representation, not the CP/CPN approximation.

class VeraGridEngine.Simulations.Rms.problems.rms_problem_phasor.RmsProblemPhasor(grid: MultiCircuit, options: RmsOptions, pf_results: PowerFlowResults | None, progress_signal: DummySignal | None = None)[source]

Bases: RmsProblemTemplate

Phasor-based DAE (Differential-Algebraic Equation) class.

This class uses phasor representation (Vr, Vi) for voltages instead of polar coordinates (Vm, Va). The phasor representation makes current equations linear and is more suitable for certain analysis.

Responsibilities:

  • Store state and algebraic variables (x, y) using phasor representation

  • Store Jacobian matrices

  • Store residual equations using phasor-based power flow equations

  • Store sparsity patterns

  • Convert between polar (power flow) and phasor (RMS) representations

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.Rms.problems.rms_problem_template.project_initial_algebraic_state(problem: RmsProblemTemplate, initial_values: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], differential_values: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], tolerance: float, max_iter: int) → Tuple[ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], bool, float][source]

Project an RMS initial vector onto its algebraic constraint manifold.

Explicit inc(...) equations seed controller states, while the remaining algebraic variables still need a zero-time network solve. Performing that solve before the first accepted sample prevents an artificial algebraic jump from entering derivative history on the second integration step.

Parameters:

  • problem – Compiled RMS problem that owns the algebraic residual.

  • initial_values – Explicitly seeded state and algebraic vector.

  • differential_values – Initial differential-variable values.

  • tolerance – Required infinity norm of the algebraic residual.

  • max_iter – Maximum Newton projection iterations.

Returns:

Projected vector, convergence flag, and final residual norm.

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.Rms.problems.rms_problem_template.rectangular_current_from_power(power: complex, voltage: complex) → Tuple[float, float][source]

Convert one complex-power operating point to rectangular current.

The RMS injection convention is S = V * conj(I). This helper supplies the exact current seed associated with an already-converged power-flow voltage and avoids an artificial first-step residual in models that expose both power and current variables.

Parameters:

  • power – Complex injected power in per unit.

  • voltage – Complex terminal voltage in per unit.

Returns:

Real and imaginary current components in per unit.

VeraGridEngine.Simulations.Rms.problems.rms_problem_template.solve_rms_newton_correction(jacobian: csc_matrix, residual: ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]], reference_column: int | None) → ndarray[tuple[Any, ...], dtype[float64]][source]

Solve one RMS Newton system while fixing an explicit gauge coordinate.

AC RMS systems can retain one global voltage-angle coordinate while exposing one fewer independent residual. Appending a zero-correction constraint for the recorded reference angle makes that Newton system square without discarding any physical equation or moving the accepted reference frame.

Parameters:

  • jacobian – Newton Jacobian for the current residual vector.

  • residual – Residual vector whose correction is required.

  • reference_column – Optional Jacobian column of the fixed gauge value.

Returns:

Finite direct correction when the system is square or has one known gauge coordinate; otherwise the minimum-norm least-squares correction.
